MUTUAL NONDISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

This Mutual Nondisclosure Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of October 21, 2026 (the "Effective Date"), by and between:

(1) Veloce Cloud Technologies, Inc., a Delaware corporation with its principal executive offices at 500 Delaware Avenue, Suite 1100, Wilmington, DE 19801 ("Veloce"); and

(2) Halyard Software Ltd, a company incorporated and registered in England and Wales with company number 09876543, whose registered office is at 12 Mill Lane, Manchester M1 2AB ("Halyard").

Veloce and Halyard may collectively be referred to as the "Parties," and each individually as a "Party."

RECITALS

A. The Parties wish to explore and evaluate a potential business relationship and technology collaboration relating to enterprise cloud infrastructure software integration (the "Purpose").

B. In connection with the Purpose, each Party may disclose to the other Party certain non-public, proprietary, or confidential information, and the Parties desire to establish terms governing the protection, use, and disclosure of such information.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants contained herein and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

Certain Definitions

1.1 "Affiliate" means, with respect to any specified entity, any other entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such entity, where "control" means the ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the outstanding voting securities or equity interests of such entity.

1.2 "Applicable Law" means any statute, law, ordinance, regulation, rule, code, or judicial order enacted, adopted, or issued by any governmental or regulatory authority of competent jurisdiction.

1.3 "Confidential Information" means any and all proprietary, technical, operational, commercial, or business information disclosed by or on behalf of a Disclosing Party to a Receiving Party under this Agreement, whether disclosed orally, visually, electronically, or in tangible form, including without limitation source code, software architecture, object code, API specifications, product plans, benchmark results, customer lists, financial forecasts, pricing policies, and trade secrets, that is designated as confidential at the time of disclosure or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential given the nature of the information or the circumstances surrounding disclosure.

1.4 "Disclosing Party" means the Party disclosing Proprietary or Confidential Information hereunder.

1.5 "Receiving Party" means the Party receiving Proprietary or Confidential Information hereunder.

1.6 "Representatives" means a Party's and its Affiliates' directors, officers, employees, legal counsel, accountants, and financial advisors.

Confidentiality Obligations and Restrictive Covenants

2.1 The Receiving Party shall hold all Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party in strict confidence and shall not disclose, publish, or disseminate such Confidential Information to any third party, except as expressly permitted under Section 3.

2.2 The Receiving Party shall protect the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information with the same degree of care that it uses to protect its own confidential information of like kind, but in no event less than a reasonable degree of care, and shall use such Confidential Information solely to evaluate and perform the Purpose.

2.3 The Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, or derive the composition, structure, or source code of any hardware, software, or samples furnished by the Disclosing Party.

2.4 In order to protect the Disclosing Party's legitimate proprietary interests and goodwill in its proprietary cloud software platform and enterprise market relationships disclosed during the evaluation of the Purpose, the Receiving Party covenants and agrees that, during the term of this Agreement and for a period of twelve (12) months following any termination or expiration hereof, the Receiving Party shall not, directly or indirectly, whether as principal, agent, partner, consultant, or otherwise, develop, market, distribute, license, or sell any software product, service, or feature that directly competes with the enterprise cloud infrastructure solutions disclosed by the Disclosing Party, nor shall the Receiving Party enter into any commercial partnership, joint venture, or distribution arrangement with any direct competitor of the Disclosing Party in respect of the subject matter evaluated under the Purpose.

Permitted Disclosures and Exceptions

3.1 The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information only to those of its Representatives who need to know such information for the Purpose and who are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as restrictive as those contained in this Agreement. The Receiving Party shall be fully liable for any breach of this Agreement by any of its Representatives.

3.2 The obligations set forth in Section 2.1 and Section 2.2 shall not apply to any information that the Receiving Party can establish by competent written proof:

3.2.1 is or becomes publicly known through no breach of this Agreement by the Receiving Party or its Representatives;

3.2.2 was already in the lawful possession of the Receiving Party without confidentiality restrictions prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party;

3.2.3 is received from a third party without breach of any confidentiality obligation owed to the Disclosing Party; or

3.2.4 is independently developed by the Receiving Party without reference to, reliance upon, or use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.

Legally Compelled Disclosures

4.1 If the Receiving Party is requested or required pursuant to Applicable Law, valid subpoena, court order, or regulatory process to disclose any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, the Receiving Party shall, to the extent legally permissible, provide the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice thereof so that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy.

4.2 The Receiving Party shall cooperate reasonably with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party's expense, in seeking such protective measures. If such protective order or other remedy is not obtained, the Receiving Party shall disclose only that portion of the Confidential Information that it is legally advised it is compelled to disclose.

Return and Retention of Materials

5.1 Upon written request of the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party shall promptly, and in any event within fifteen (15) days of receipt of such request, securely destroy or return to the Disclosing Party all materials, documents, and records containing or reflecting any Confidential Information, together with all copies thereof, and shall certify compliance in writing.

5.2 Notwithstanding Section 5.1, the Receiving Party may retain copies of Confidential Information to the extent required to satisfy statutory document-retention mandates, or to the extent stored on routine, automated electronic backup systems, provided that all such retained Confidential Information shall remain subject to the terms of this Agreement until destroyed.

Intellectual Property and Warranty Disclaimer

6.1 All Confidential Information remains the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party. Nothing herein shall be construed as granting any right, title, license, or interest by implication, estoppel, or otherwise in or to any patent, trademark, copyright, trade secret, or other intellectual property right of the Disclosing Party.

6.2 All Confidential Information is provided on an "as is" and "with all faults" basis, without any warranties of any kind, whether express, implied, statutory, or otherwise, regarding its accuracy, completeness, non-infringement, or fitness for a particular purpose.

Indemnification and Remedies

7.1 The Receiving Party agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Disclosing Party, its Affiliates, and their respective directors, officers, employees, and agents from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, judgments, fines, penalties, settlements, costs, and expenses (including without limitation court costs and reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses) arising out of, resulting from, or relating to any breach or alleged breach of this Agreement, or any unauthorized use, disclosure, or misappropriation of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information by the Receiving Party or any of its Representatives, without any monetary cap or other limitation of liability whatsoever.

7.2 The Parties acknowledge that unauthorized disclosure or use of Confidential Information will cause immediate, substantial, and irreparable harm for which compensatory damages would be difficult to quantify and inadequate to compensate the Disclosing Party. Consequently, in the event of any material breach or threatened material breach of Section 2 of this Agreement by the Receiving Party or its Representatives, the Receiving Party shall pay to the Disclosing Party, immediately upon written demand, the sum of one hundred thousand United States dollars ($100,000) for each such breach or unauthorized disclosure event as agreed liquidated damages and not as a penalty, representing a reasonable pre-estimate of administrative and operational investigation costs, without prejudice to the Disclosing Party's right to seek further injunctive or other equitable relief in respect thereof.

7.3 Each Party acknowledges that monetary relief alone may not be sufficient for any actual or threatened violation of this Agreement, and each Party shall be entitled to seek immediate injunctive relief and specific performance, without posting bond or proving actual damages, in addition to all other rights and remedies available to it under this Agreement or at law.

Term and Termination

8.1 This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in effect for a term of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Party.

8.2 The obligations of nondisclosure and non-use with respect to Confidential Information shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of such expiration or termination, provided that with respect to any Confidential Information constituting a trade secret under Applicable Law, such obligations shall continue indefinitely for as long as such information remains a trade secret.

Miscellaneous Provisions

9.1 Governing Law and Jurisdiction. This Agreement and any dispute or claim (including non-contractual disputes or claims) arising out of or in connection with it or its subject matter or formation shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of England and Wales. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales to resolve any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement.

9.2 Entire Agreement. This Agreement constitutes the complete and exclusive understanding between the Parties concerning the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous proposals, understandings, and agreements, whether oral or written.

9.3 Amendments. No amendment, modification, or waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless set forth in a written instrument duly executed by authorized signatories of both Parties.

9.4 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable under Applicable Law, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision hereof, and this Agreement shall be reformed and construed to the maximum extent permitted by law.

9.5 Assignment. Neither Party may assign or transfer this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other Party, except that either Party may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor entity in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all of its assets.

9.6 Notices. All notices required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be delivered by internationally recognized courier service, registered mail, or electronic transmission with confirmed receipt to the respective addresses set forth above.

9.7 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart via electronic signature or portable document format (PDF) shall be deemed valid and binding.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Mutual Nondisclosure Agreement as of the Effective Date.
